title: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid VIII (ACSF.VIII)
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Calcium Chloride, dihydrate (CaCl2·2 H2O) (Sigma C3881, C3306 or equivalent)
D-Glucose (C6H12O6; aka Dextrose) (Sigma G7021, Sigma G8270 or equivalent)
Magnesium Sulfate, Heptahydrate (MgSO4·7 H2O) (Sigma M1880 or equivalent)
Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH2PO4 • H2O) (Sigma S9638 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (KCl) (Sigma P9333, P5405, P4504 or equivalent)
Sodium L-Ascorbate (C6H7NaO6 ) (Sigma A7631, A4034 or equivalent)
Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3) (Sigma S5761, VWR MK739604 or equivalent)
P200 pipette tips (Rainin GPL200F or equivalent)
P1000 pipette tips (Rainin GPL1000F or equivalent)
Osmometer sample tubes (Advanced Instruments 3LA825 or equivalent)

steps.title: Prepare reagent stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required stock solutions and store them as indicated.

substeps.instruction: Calcium Chloride dihydrate 200 mM: dissolve 29.4 g CaCl2·2H2O in 900 mL MilliQ water, top to 1 L, store at room temperature up to 60 days.
HEPES 1 M: dissolve 238.3 g HEPES in 900 mL MilliQ water, top to 1 L, store at room temperature up to 60 days.
Magnesium Sulfate heptahydrate 1 M: dissolve 246 g MgSO4·7H2O in 900 mL MilliQ water, top to 1 L, store at room temperature up to 60 days.
Sodium Chloride 4 M: dissolve 233.8 g NaCl in 900 mL MilliQ water, top to 1 L, store at room temperature up to 60 days.
Sodium Pyruvate 500 mM: dissolve 55 g CH3COCOONa in 900 mL MilliQ water, top to 1 L, store at 4 °C up to 60 days.
Thiourea 1.6 M: dissolve 6.08 g thiourea in 40 mL MilliQ water, top to 50 mL, aliquot 5–7 mL into 15 mL conical tubes, store at –20 °C up to 60 days (warm to room temperature before use).

steps.title: Label containers and obtain stir bar
steps.instruction: Label a sterile 1 L polystyrene bottle with reagent name, date and preparer’s initials; obtain an RNase‑free stir bar and place it in the container.

steps.title: Set up stirring equipment
steps.instruction: Set up a magnetic stir plate inside a fume hood and place the RNase‑free container with stir bar on it.

steps.title: Determine ACSF volume to prepare
steps.instruction: Consult the reagent request form to decide whether to prepare 500 mL or 1 L of ACSF.VIII (the steps below describe the 1 L preparation).

steps.title: Standard 1 L ACSF.VIII preparation
steps.instruction: Combine water, stock solutions and solid reagents in the labeled RNase‑free container, adjust pH, add calcium and magnesium stocks, set final volume, and verify osmolarity.

substeps.instruction: Measure 600 mL MilliQ water with a graduated cylinder and add to the labeled RNase‑free container containing the stir bar.
Place the container on the stir plate and set the speed to high (setting 7 or higher).
Add 20 mL of the 1 M HEPES stock solution using a sterile serological pipette or graduated cylinder.
Weigh 186 mg potassium chloride (KCl) on a calibrated balance and add slowly while stirring.
Weigh 166 mg sodium phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH2PO4·H2O) and add slowly while stirring.
Add 23 mL of the 4 M sodium chloride stock solution.
Add 6 mL of the 500 mM sodium pyruvate stock solution.
Add 1.25 mL of the 1.6 M thiourea stock solution (ensure it is at room temperature).
Weigh 4.5 g D‑glucose and add slowly while stirring.
Weigh 990 mg sodium L‑ascorbate and add slowly while stirring.
Weigh 2.52 g sodium bicarbonate and add slowly while stirring.
Continue stirring at high speed (setting 7 or higher) until all components are fully dissolved.
Measure pH with a calibrated pH meter and adjust to 7.3 using NaOH (add dropwise as needed).
Add 10 mL of the 200 mM calcium chloride stock solution.
Add 2 mL of the 1 M magnesium sulfate stock solution.
Remove the stir bar with a magnetic stir bar remover.
Adjust the final volume to exactly 1000 mL with MilliQ water using the graduation marks on the container or a graduated cylinder.
Measure osmolarity:
• If using a 3250 Freezing Point Osmometer, measure a 250 µL sample; target 305–315 mOsm (305–315 mmol/kg).
• If using a Vapro 5600 Osmometer, measure a 10 µL sample; target 300–310 mOsm (300–310 mmol/kg).
If osmolarity is too high, add MilliQ water; if too low, add the calculated volume X of 1 mg/mL NaCl solution (X = volume in mL). Re‑measure and confirm the target range.
Filter the ACSF through a Corning 1 L 0.45 µm filter system:
• Attach the filter system to a Gast DOA‑P104‑AA vacuum pump using Tygon tubing and turn on the pump.
• Filter 500 mL at a time while continuously stirring the remaining solution on the stir plate.
Label the final bottle with reagent name, date, time and preparer’s initials.
Record the preparation date, lot numbers of all components and the measured osmolarity in the reagent preparation notebook.
Dispose of any excess reagent directly into the municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with RNase Away and rinse thoroughly with MilliQ water.
Store the completed ACSF at 4 °C and use within 24 hours.

steps.title: Rapid 1 L ACSF.VIII preparation
steps.instruction: Use concentrated 2 M calcium and magnesium stocks to prepare a liquid stock, then add solid components from a conical tube, filter, and adjust pH, volume and osmolarity.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 2 M calcium chloride dihydrate stock: dissolve 14.7 g CaCl2·2H2O in 30 mL MilliQ water, bring to 50 mL total volume, transfer to a labeled 250 mL polystyrene bottle, store at room temperature up to 60 days.

Prepare 2 M magnesium sulfate heptahydrate stock: dissolve 24.65 g MgSO4·7H2O in 30 mL MilliQ water, bring to 50 mL total volume, transfer to a labeled 250 mL polystyrene bottle, store at room temperature up to 60 days.
Label a sterile 1 L polystyrene bottle with reagent name, date and preparer’s initials; obtain an RNase‑free stir bar and place it in the bottle.
Add approximately 500 mL MilliQ water to a 1000 mL beaker.
Place the stir bar in the beaker and set the stir plate to a medium speed (setting 4–7).
Weigh 4.77 g HEPES and add to the beaker.
Using a disposable transfer pipette, add 13–14 drops of 5 N NaOH to the beaker.
Add 1 mL of the 2 M magnesium sulfate stock using a P1000 pipette.
Add 1 mL of the 2 M calcium chloride stock using a P1000 pipette.
Remove the stir bar, adjust the volume to 950 mL with MilliQ water, and pour the liquid into a sterile 1000 mL bottle (this is the liquid stock).
Obtain a 50 mL conical tube, place it in a tube holder, and weigh out and add the solid components listed in Table 2 (use a new weigh boat and disposable spatula for each reagent).
Set the tube aside and obtain a 1 L 0.45 µm filter system.
Attach the vacuum pump to the filter system and filter the liquid stock into a fresh 1000 mL bottle.

Label both the solid‑component tube and the liquid‑stock bottle with contents, preparation date, expiration date and initials; tape the conical tube to the side of the bottle and store at 4 °C for up to 60 days.
Pour the solid contents from the conical tube into the liquid‑stock bottle, secure the cap and shake vigorously to mix.
When powder remains, pour ~40–45 mL of ACSF.VIII into the conical tube, then back into the bottle; repeat 2–3 times until no residue remains, shaking after each cycle.
Add a stir bar to the bottle and measure pH while stirring on a stir plate; acceptable pH is 7.3–7.4.
If pH is too high, add 5 N HCl dropwise; if pH is too low, add 5 N NaOH dropwise. Remove the stir bar when the target pH is reached.
Adjust the final volume to exactly 1000 mL with MilliQ water using the graduation marks or a graduated cylinder.
Measure osmolarity with a calibrated freezing‑point osmometer (250 µL sample); acceptable range is 305–315 mOsm.
After each reading, rinse the probe with MilliQ water, dry with a kimwipe, and clean gently with a wet kimwipe (MilliQ water only) before the next test.
If osmolarity is too high, add a small amount of MilliQ water; if too low, add the calculated volume X of 1 mg/mL NaCl solution (X = volume in mL). Re‑measure and confirm the target range.
Filter the final ACSF through the 0.45 µm filter system; optionally perform a sterile 0.22 µm filtration if the solution will be used for slice culture.
